key.lifecycle: loaded from the managed policy source at startup (with live reload on change); governs which permission modes are selectable for the whole session
key.failure_mode: The guarantee is only as strong as the OS ACLs on the managed file location and the reach of the deployment tooling: a developer with local admin rights, or a laptop the MDM never touched, is outside the control.

sheets.primary: Managed policy settings deployed fleet-wide via MDM (macOS com.anthropic.claudecode plist, Windows HKLM registry) or a system managed-settings.json (/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/, /etc/claude-code/, C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\), setting permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable" and optionally disableAutoMode.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Putting disableBypassPermissionsMode in user or project settings.json: the key works from any scope, but a developer can simply edit those files, so only the managed scope satisfies 'cannot lift it from home directory or repo'.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness: managed settings sit at the top of the precedence order and cannot be overridden by user settings, project settings, or command-line arguments.
sheets.context_boundary: Pure configuration evaluated at startup and on mode switches; nothing enters the model context beyond the refusal when bypass mode is attempted.
sheets.lifecycle: Applied at every session start on every machine that carries the policy (SessionEnd even has a bypass_permissions_disabled reason); it stays in force until IT withdraws the policy.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open per machine that never received the profile or file: a laptop missing the policy has no restriction; mitigate with server-managed settings plus forceRemoteSettingsRefresh for fail-closed startup, and keep file-based policy in admin-only paths so users cannot edit it.
sheets.version_caveat: The legacy C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json path is unsupported as of v2.1.75 (migrate to C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode); server-managed delivery and forceRemoteSettingsRefresh require the claude.ai admin console or a self-hosted Claude apps gateway.

sheets.primary: Managed policy settings deployed fleet-wide by IT (MDM profile, HKLM registry policy, server-managed settings, or a system managed-settings.json) setting permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable". Managed settings sit at the top of precedence, so nothing in a home directory, repo, or command line can lift the restriction.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Putting the same key in user or project settings.json: the setting works from any scope, but a developer owns those files and can simply delete the line, which fails the requirement that the control survive edits to anything the developer controls.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness: Claude Code refuses to enter bypassPermissions mode based on the managed policy, independent of anything the model or user requests; managed settings cannot be overridden by any other level including command line arguments.
sheets.context_boundary: Nothing runs in any context window; this is harness configuration evaluated at settings load. The model never sees or reasons about the policy.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies at every session start and on live settings reload for as long as the managed source is deployed on the laptop; it stops applying only when IT removes it from the managed channel.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open on any laptop where no managed source was actually deployed, so fleet coverage is the weak point; for remote delivery, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh makes startup fail closed if the managed settings fetch fails. On managed machines the control fails closed: bypass mode is simply unavailable.
sheets.version_caveat: On Windows the legacy managed settings path is dead: files must live at C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json because the C:\ProgramData location is unsupported as of v2.1.75.

sheets.primary: Enterprise managed policy settings: an MDM-deployed managed-settings.json in the system location (C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode on Windows, /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode on macOS, /etc/claude-code on Linux) setting disableBypassPermissionsMode to disable, which blocks bypassPermissions and --dangerously-skip-permissions fleet-wide.
sheets.rejected_alternative: User or project settings.json: those sit below the managed tier in precedence and are exactly the files a developer can edit, so they cannot meet the tamper requirement.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Harness: the CLI refuses to enter bypass mode when the managed policy forbids it, regardless of flags, home-directory config, or repo config.
sheets.context_boundary: Pure configuration enforcement at startup and mode-switch time inside the harness; nothing runs in or crosses into the model's context window.
sheets.lifecycle: Read at every session start from the system path; managed settings take highest precedence over CLI flags and local, project, and user settings, and apply until IT removes or changes the MDM-deployed file.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open per machine: a laptop the MDM missed has no control, a developer with local admin rights can delete the system file, and the policy only governs Claude Code itself, not some other agent binary the developer might run.
sheets.version_caveat: Managed settings and the disableBypassPermissionsMode key are 2025-era Claude Code features; I am confident of the key's purpose but not of the exact version that introduced it.

sheets.primary: Managed policy settings deployed fleet-wide through MDM (macOS managed preferences, Windows HKLM policy registry key, or a system managed-settings.json, or server-managed settings) setting permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode to "disable". Settled by the tamper-boundary axis: enforcement that must survive the user's own edits requires the managed tier.
sheets.rejected_alternative: The same disableBypassPermissionsMode key in checked-in project or user settings: mechanically it works from any scope, but a developer can edit those files, failing the requirement that nothing in the home directory or a controlled repo can lift the restriction.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness, at the managed-policy tier: the permission mode gate is enforced by Claude Code's configuration layer and admin-deployed managed settings cannot be overridden from below.
sheets.context_boundary: Enforced in the harness configuration layer at startup and on any attempted mode switch; no context window is involved and the model neither sees nor influences the policy.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies to every session on every machine carrying the deployed policy, from startup; user, project and local settings and CLI flags cannot override it, and it stops only when IT withdraws the managed policy.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed on managed machines: bypassPermissions cannot be activated. The practical failure is coverage, since a laptop where MDM never delivered the policy silently fails open; note invalid managed entries are stripped tolerantly rather than disabling the rest of policy, and user-writable HKCU-only delivery does not satisfy the tamper requirement.
sheets.version_caveat: On Windows the legacy C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json path is unsupported as of v2.1.75; deploy to C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json or the HKLM policy key instead.
